questions.q: How do teams differ from manual sharing, per this lesson?
options: Teams are a one-time grant; manual sharing is standing and reusable
Teams provide standing, reusable collaboration for a defined group; manual sharing is a one-off grant on a single record
Teams only work on custom objects
There is no meaningful difference between them
questions.explain: The lesson frames teams as the standing, reusable counterpart to manual sharing's one-off, single-record grant.

questions.q: What two things are set independently per team member when adding them to a team?
options: Their profile and their permission set
Their Team Role and their Access Level on the record
Their organization-wide default and their role hierarchy position
Their login hours and password policy
questions.explain: Each team member gets a free-text Team Role plus an independent Access Level (Read Only or Read/Write).

questions.q: What does 'Add Default Team' let a user do, per this lesson?
options: Delete all existing team members from a record
Pull in a pre-configured standard team automatically, instead of re-adding the same people one by one
Convert an Opportunity Team into an Account Team
Grant View All on the object to every team member
questions.explain: Default Team lets a pre-configured team be added to a new record in one click rather than rebuilding it each time.

questions.q: How do Account Teams, Opportunity Teams, and Case Teams relate to each other, per this lesson?
options: They are three unrelated features with nothing in common
The same underlying pattern -- role and access level per member -- applied to three different objects
Only Opportunity Teams actually grant record access; the others are cosmetic
Case Teams replace the need for Account and Opportunity Teams
questions.explain: The lesson describes all three as the same mechanics applied to Account, Opportunity, and Case records respectively.

questions.q: How do Opportunity Splits differ from Opportunity Teams, per this lesson?
options: Splits allocate revenue credit among team members; Teams grant record access -- different problems on the same record
Splits and Teams are the exact same feature under two names
Splits replace the need for an Opportunity Team entirely
Splits control field-level security on the Opportunity
questions.explain: The lesson distinguishes Splits (revenue credit allocation) from Teams (record access) even though both appear on the same Opportunity.
